cards.claim: The JEE (Advanced) 2026 syllabus lists 'projectiles' under two-dimensional kinematics (Cartesian coordinates only) but does not name projection on an inclined plane. This extension is therefore covered only under the general 'projectiles' heading, not named in the syllabus.
cards.quote: Kinematics in one and two dimensions (Cartesian coordinates only), projectiles; Uniform circular motion; Relative velocity.

locator.section: JEE (Advanced) 2026 Information Brochure, Syllabus — Physics, Mechanics

cards.claim: For projection on an incline, take x along the plane and y perpendicular to it, resolve g into components along and perpendicular to the plane, and solve the two motions independently with time as the common parameter.
cards.quote: (ii) We can take x-dir ection along the plane and y-direction perpendicular to the plane. In that case resolve g (acceleration due to gravity) in two differrent components, gx along the plane and gy perpendicular to the plane. Now the problem can be solved as two independent motions in x and y directions respectively with time as a common parameter.)

cards.claim: Alternatively, the landing point on the incline is the intersection of the parabolic trajectory with the straight line of the plane.
cards.quote: (i) Point P at which particle hits the plane can be seen as intersection of its trajectory (parobola) and straight line.

cards.claim: The constant-acceleration vector equations do not depend on a choice of axes and can be resolved along any two independent axes, such as axes along and perpendicular to an incline.
cards.quote: The vector equations (3.33a) and (3.34a) do not involve any choice of axes. Of course, you can always resolve them along any two independent axes.

cards.claim: The level-ground time-of-flight formula does not apply when the projectile lands at a different elevation from its launch point, as it does on an incline.
cards.quote: Equation 4.24 does not apply when the projectile lands at a different elevation than it was launched

cards.claim: NCERT Exemplar 4.31: a particle projected at beta to a surface inclined at alpha; find the range on the plane, the time of flight, and the beta for maximum range.
cards.quote: A particle is projected in air at an angle β to a surface which itself is inclined at an angle α to the horizontal (Fig. 4.6). (a) Find an expression of range on the plane surface (distance on the plane from the point of projection at which particle will hit the surface). (b) Time of flight. (c) β at which range will be maximum.

cards.claim: JEE (Advanced) 2026 Paper 1 Q6: a particle is thrown with speed v from O at angle theta to the horizontal and passes through P, 1 m high and 5 m horizontally from O; g in m/s^2. Which are correct: (A) if theta = 45 degrees, v = 5 sqrt(g)/2 m/s; (B) if theta = 45 degrees, it reaches maximum height before P; (C) if theta = 30 degrees, it reaches maximum height after P; (D) if theta = tan^-1(1/5), v = 125 sqrt(g) m/s (fractions flattened in the PDF text; see equation).
cards.quote: A particle is thrown with a speed 𝑣 from a point 𝑂 at an angle 𝜃 with the horizontal plane such that it passes through the point 𝑃 at a height of 1 m and horizontal distance of 5 m from 𝑂, as shown in the figure. If acceleration due to gravity is 𝑔 ms−2, then the correct statement(s) is/are: (A) If 𝜃 = 45o, then 𝑣 = 5√𝑔 2  ms−1. (B) If 𝜃 = 45o, the particle reaches its maximum height before it reaches 𝑃. (C) If 𝜃 = 30o, the particle reaches its maximum height after reaching 𝑃. (D) If 𝜃 = tan−1 ( 1 5), then 𝑣 = 125√𝑔 ms−1.
cards.equation: (A)\ \theta=45^\circ\Rightarrow v=\tfrac{5\sqrt g}{2};\ (D)\ \theta=\tan^{-1}(1/5)\Rightarrow v=125\sqrt g\ \text{(as printed in the text layer)}

cards.claim: JEE (Advanced) 2026 Paper 1 final answer for Q6: options A and B.
cards.quote: then the correct statement(s) is/are: (A) If 𝜃 = 45o, then 𝑣 = 5√𝑔 2 ms−1. (B) If 𝜃 = 45o, the particle reaches its maximum height before it reaches 𝑃. (C) If 𝜃 = 30o, the particle reaches its maximum height after reaching 𝑃. (D) If 𝜃 = tan−1 ( 1 5), then 𝑣 = 125√𝑔 ms−1. Answer Q6: AB
